definition: A Recognition Memory Test is a memory assessment that asks a person to identify previously encountered items, such as faces or words, from among alternatives. In this source, the Warrington Recognition Memory Test is used especially to measure facial memory as an aspect of visual memory.

reasons: The definition’s general description (“asks a person to identify previously encountered items…from among alternatives”) is not explicitly supported anywhere in the provided packet text.

The packet supports that the Warrington Recognition Memory Test for Faces (RMF) is used to evaluate facial memory/visual memory in this study, but it does not provide enough information to support the broader “recognition memory test” definition as written.

The packet supports the Warrington Recognition Memory Test as a word-and-face memory measure, but it does not support the general definition that a recognition memory test asks a person to identify previously encountered items ‘from among alternatives.’
The packet supports use of the test for facial memory/visual memory in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy, but the definition broadens beyond what is stated in the source without clear support.
